s: A company plans to refactor a monolithic application into a modern application designed deployed or AWS. The CLCD pipeline needs to be upgraded to support the modem design for the application with the following requirements It should allow changes to be released several times every hour. * It should be able to roll back the changes as quickly as possible. Which design will meet these requirements?
o: Deploy a Cl-CD pipeline that incorporates AMIs to contain the application and their configurations Deploy the application by replacing Amazon EC2 instances
Specify AWS Elastic Beanstak to sage in a secondary environment as the deployment target for the CI/CD pipeline of the application. To deploy swap the staging and production environment URLs.

Use AWS Systems Manager to re-provision the infrastructure for each deployment Update the Amazon EC2 user data to pull the latest code art-fact from Amazon S3 and use Amazon Route 53 weighted routing to point to the new environment

Roll out the application updates as pan of an Auto Scaling event using prebuilt AMIs. Use new versions of the AMIs to add instances, and phase out all instances that use the previous AMI version with the configured termination policy during a deployment event.
e: It is the fastest when it comes to rollback and deploying changes every hour

w.y: Release several times an hour and roll back as fast as possible. Elastic Beanstalk blue/green with a CNAME swap switches traffic in one step, and swapping back is just as fast.

o.A: Wrong: baking AMIs and replacing instances is slow for both release and rollback.
o.B: Correct: a staging environment plus a URL swap gives quick releases and an instant rollback.
o.C: Wrong: rebuilding infrastructure on each deployment is slow, and DNS changes wait on TTLs.
o.D: Wrong: rolling AMI replacement is slow, and rollback means rolling out instances again.
